items.title: Hitachi EX5500-6 mining excavator passes 100,000 hours at Moatize
items.summary: The mine is operated by Vulcan Mozambique SA. To celebrate this achievement, a ceremony was held at the mine on August 27. Approximately 80 Vulcan and Hitachi Construction Machinery Group officials attended the ceremony, where appreciation was expressed and recognition given to the operators, engineers, and maintenance staff who have supported the machine’s operation for many years Vulcan operates the Moatize Coal Mine and is a global company with operations spanning more than 25 countries and six continents. As one of Mozambique’s leading mining companies, Vulcan engages in coal mining and supply and contributes to the country’s industry and job creation The EX5500-6 that achieved this milestone was delivered in June 2010 and reached a cumulative 100,000 hours of operation in July 2026.

items.title: Israel election: Israelis vote for 1st time since October 7 terror attack
items.summary: Israel's longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, faces a battle to stay in power amid fierce competition from a bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot. Arab parties are projected to play kingmakers Follow below for all the latest on the Israeli election on October 27, 2026, and its aftermath: While the main competition for the largest number of seats is between Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud and Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar, the Arab parties are projected to play a key role in determining Israel's next ruling coalition For a party or coalition to rule, it needs to secure 61 seats in the Knesset As per a recent Channel 12 poll, Eisenkot's bloc is hovering around 55 seats, while Netanyahu's bloc is trailing behind with some 51 seats. This means that either bloc would need to form coalitions in order to rule, should the election results come out similar to the polls The most likely parties to tip the scales are the Joint List (projected to win around 9 seats) and the Ra'am (projected to win around 5 seats).

items.title: Israel heads to polls for pivotal election defined by security and democracy
items.summary: Polling published on Friday suggests Gadi Eisenkot (left) is in a tight race with incumbent Benjamin Netanyahu (right) Israelis are heading to the polls for what many view as one of the most pivotal elections in the country's history Polling published on Friday suggests incumbent Benjamin Netanyahu is in a near neck-and-neck race with former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to become prime minister But neither of their political blocs are projected to win the 61 seats needed to form a majority government - meaning weeks or months of political wrangling may lie ahead The campaign has been shaped by the issue of security - with the opposition bloc hammering Netanyahu for the unprecedented security failure that led to the 7 October Hamas-led attacks on Israel, in which nearly 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken back to Gaza as hostages They have pushed for an independent commission of inquiry into the attacks - something Netanyahu has long resisted, insisting it would be biased against him Despite the opposition's attack lines, Netanyahu has once again framed himself as "Mr Security" -…

items.title: Nurse killed in attack while responding to Ebola alert in DR Congo
items.summary: A nurse has been killed and another health worker seriously injured in an attack as they were responding to an Ebola alert in north-eastern Democratic Republic of Congo The two were targeted by local youths who accused them of contaminating water sources and spreading the Ebola virus, according to the UN-backed Radio Okapi.
